/-!
# Conjecture 4.6

by V. A. Artamonov

(P. Hall). Are the projective groups in the variety of metabelian groups free?

A group $G$ is *metabelian* if its derived subgroup $G'$ is abelian, i.e. $G'' = 1$.
The metabelian groups form a variety of groups. A group $P$ is *projective* in this
variety if it is metabelian and every homomorphism $P \to B$ into a metabelian group $B$
lifts along every surjective homomorphism $A \to B$ of metabelian groups; equivalently,
$P$ is a retract of a free metabelian group. "Free" means free in the variety, i.e.
isomorphic to a *free metabelian group* $F/F''$ for an (absolutely) free group $F$ of
arbitrary rank. (An absolutely free group of rank at least $2$ is not metabelian.)

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable` (too weak: any derived length), `derivedSeries`/`commutator G` (used as the building block), `IsMulCommutative (commutator G)` (equivalent alternative formulation; the derived-series form was chosen because it is shorter and matches the notebook's variety-of-groups language).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.6».IsMetabelian
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no predicate for metabelian groups (G'' = 1). Defined as `derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥`, which is exactly `⁅G', G'⁆ = 1`, i.e. the derived subgroup is abelian.

/-- A group $G$ is *metabelian* if its derived subgroup $G'$ is abelian, i.e. $G'' = 1$:
the second term of the derived series of $G$ is trivial. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥

def IsFreeMetabelian (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ X : Type u, Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup X ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2)
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *free metabelian*, i.e. free in the variety of metabelian groups, if it is
isomorphic to $F/F''$ for some absolutely free group $F$ (of any rank, possibly zero or
infinite).

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsFreeGroup` / `IsFreeGroupBasis` (absolutely free — wrong variety), `Abelianization` (only for the abelian variety).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.6».IsFreeMetabelian
justification.why_needed: 'Free' in the problem means free in the variety of metabelian groups, i.e. isomorphic to F/F'' for an absolutely free group F. Mathlib only has absolutely free groups (`IsFreeGroup`, `FreeGroup`), and an absolutely free group of rank ≥ 2 is not metabelian, so a relatively free notion was needed. Defined as `∃ X : Type u, Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup X ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2)`; rank X is arbitrary (zero, finite, or infinite).

blocks.name: IsFreeMetabelian
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *free metabelian*, i.e. free in the variety of metabelian groups, if it is
isomorphic to $F/F''$ for some absolutely free group $F$ (of any rank, possibly zero or
infinite). -/
def IsFreeMetabelian (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ X : Type u, Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup X ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2)

def IsProjectiveMetabelian (P : Type u) [Group P] : Prop :=
  IsMetabelian P ∧
    ∀ (A B : Type u) [Group A] [Group B], IsMetabelian A → IsMetabelian B →
      ∀ f : A →* B, Function.Surjective f → ∀ g : P →* B, ∃ h : P →* A, f.comp h = g
blocks.docstring:
A group $P$ is *projective in the variety of metabelian groups* if it is metabelian and
for every surjective homomorphism $f \colon A \to B$ of metabelian groups and every
homomorphism $g \colon P \to B$ there is a homomorphism $h \colon P \to A$ with
$f \circ h = g$. Equivalently, $P$ is a retract of a free metabelian group.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `CategoryTheory.Projective` on `Grp` (wrong category: projectives in all groups are the absolutely free groups), `Module.Projective` (modules, not groups).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.6».IsProjectiveMetabelian
justification.why_needed: No category of metabelian groups exists in Mathlib, so `CategoryTheory.Projective` cannot be used directly (and its epimorphisms would be categorical epis rather than the surjective homomorphisms used in the group-theoretic literature). Defined as: P is metabelian, and for every surjective homomorphism f : A → B of metabelian groups and every g : P → B there is h : P → A with f ∘ h = g. This is the standard definition of a projective group in a variety and is equivalent to P being a retract of a free metabelian group (as the decomposition notes say); the file proves free metabelian groups are projective in this sense as an API test.

blocks.name: IsProjectiveMetabelian
blocks.text:
/-- A group $P$ is *projective in the variety of metabelian groups* if it is metabelian and
for every surjective homomorphism $f \colon A \to B$ of metabelian groups and every
homomorphism $g \colon P \to B$ there is a homomorphism $h \colon P \to A$ with
$f \circ h = g$. Equivalently, $P$ is a retract of a free metabelian group. -/
def IsProjectiveMetabelian (P : Type u) [Group P] : Prop :=
  IsMetabelian P ∧
    ∀ (A B : Type u) [Group A] [Group B], IsMetabelian A → IsMetabelian B →
      ∀ f : A →* B, Function.Surjective f → ∀ g : P →* B, ∃ h : P →* A, f.comp h = g

theorem kourovka.«4.6» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsProjectiveMetabelian G → IsFreeMetabelian G := by
  sorry

That is, is every group that is projective in the variety of metabelian groups a free
metabelian group $F/F''$ (of some, not necessarily finite, rank)? Here "projective" and
"free" are both relative to the variety of metabelian groups.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFreeMetabelian.isProjectiveMetabelian {G : Type u} [Group G]
    (h : IsFreeMetabelian G) : IsProjectiveMetabelian G := by
  refine ⟨h.isMetabelian, ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨X, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  intro A B _ _ hA _ f hf g
  set N := derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2
  choose a ha using fun x : X => hf (g (e.symm (QuotientGroup.mk (FreeGroup.of x))))
  have hker : N ≤ (FreeGroup.lift a).ker := by
    rw [← Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff, ← le_bot_iff, ← hA]
    exact map_derivedSeries_le_derivedSeries _ 2
  refine ⟨(QuotientGroup.lift N (FreeGroup.lift a) hker).comp e, ?_⟩
  have : f.comp (QuotientGroup.lift N (FreeGroup.lift a) hker) = g.comp e.symm := by
    refine QuotientGroup.monoidHom_ext N (FreeGroup.ext_hom _ _ fun x => ?_)
    simpa using ha x
  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x => ?_
  have h2 := DFunLike.congr_fun this (e x)
  rw [MonoidHom.comp_apply, MonoidHom.comp_apply] at h2
  simpa using h2

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question with an implicit universal quantifier over all metabelian groups (any rank, not only finitely generated): 'projective' means projective object in the category/variety of metabelian groups (equivalently a retract of a free metabelian group, i.e. every epimorphism from a metabelian group onto it splits), and 'free' means relatively free in that variety (free metabelian, F/F''), not absolutely free — an absolutely free group of rank ≥ 2 is not metabelian.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematically faithful proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G : Type, (projective in the metabelian variety) → (free in the metabelian variety), with metabelian = derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥ (G'' = 1), free-in-variety = isomorphic to FreeGroup X ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2 (F/F'' of arbitrary rank, incl. 0/infinite), projectivity = metabelian ∧ lifting/splitting against surjective homomorphisms of metabelian groups (the group-theoretic meaning in Hall/Neumann/Artamonov; equivalent to retract of a free metabelian group). answer(True) = positive answer. c02 chosen because it uses the literal categorical lifting-property definition of a projective object, has clear docstrings, and provides proved API/test lemmas for the bespoke definitions (abelian ⇒ metabelian, F/F'' is free metabelian, free metabelian ⇒ metabelian ⇒ projective) as CONTRIBUTING requests; the last also certifies the question is not vacuous. Only edit: theorem docstring now carries Hall's attribution and states both notions are relative to the variety. Compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning on the main theorem.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.6

by V. A. Artamonov

(P. Hall). Are the projective groups in the variety of metabelian groups free?

A group $G$ is *metabelian* if its derived subgroup $G'$ is abelian, i.e. $G'' = 1$.
The metabelian groups form a variety of groups. A group $P$ is *projective* in this
variety if it is metabelian and every homomorphism $P \to B$ into a metabelian group $B$
lifts along every surjective homomorphism $A \to B$ of metabelian groups; equivalently,
$P$ is a retract of a free metabelian group. "Free" means free in the variety, i.e.
isomorphic to a *free metabelian group* $F/F''$ for an (absolutely) free group $F$ of
arbitrary rank. (An absolutely free group of rank at least $2$ is not metabelian.)

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.6»

universe u

/-- A group $G$ is *metabelian* if its derived subgroup $G'$ is abelian, i.e. $G'' = 1$:
the second term of the derived series of $G$ is trivial. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥

/-- A group $G$ is *free metabelian*, i.e. free in the variety of metabelian groups, if it is
isomorphic to $F/F''$ for some absolutely free group $F$ (of any rank, possibly zero or
infinite). -/
def IsFreeMetabelian (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ X : Type u, Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup X ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2)

/-- A group $P$ is *projective in the variety of metabelian groups* if it is metabelian and
for every surjective homomorphism $f \colon A \to B$ of metabelian groups and every
homomorphism $g \colon P \to B$ there is a homomorphism $h \colon P \to A$ with
$f \circ h = g$. Equivalently, $P$ is a retract of a free metabelian group. -/
def IsProjectiveMetabelian (P : Type u) [Group P] : Prop :=
  IsMetabelian P ∧
    ∀ (A B : Type u) [Group A] [Group B], IsMetabelian A → IsMetabelian B →
      ∀ f : A →* B, Function.Surjective f → ∀ g : P →* B, ∃ h : P →* A, f.comp h = g

/-- (P. Hall). Are the projective groups in the variety of metabelian groups free?

That is, is every group that is projective in the variety of metabelian groups a free
metabelian group $F/F''$ (of some, not necessarily finite, rank)? Here "projective" and
"free" are both relative to the variety of metabelian groups. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.6» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsProjectiveMetabelian G → IsFreeMetabelian G := by
  sorry

/-- Every abelian group is metabelian. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsMetabelian G := by
  have : commutator G = ⊥ := (commutator_eq_bot_iff_center_eq_top G).mpr CommGroup.center_eq_top
  simp [IsMetabelian, derivedSeries_succ, this]

/-- A homomorphic image of a metabelian group is metabelian. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsMetabelian.of_surjective {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] (hG : IsMetabelian G)
    {f : G →* H} (hf : Function.Surjective f) : IsMetabelian H := by
  rw [IsMetabelian, ← map_derivedSeries_eq hf, hG, Subgroup.map_bot]

/-- The group $F/F''$ is free metabelian, for $F$ the free group on $X$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFreeMetabelian_quotient (X : Type u) :
    IsFreeMetabelian (FreeGroup X ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2) :=
  ⟨X, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- A free metabelian group is metabelian. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFreeMetabelian.isMetabelian {G : Type u} [Group G] (h : IsFreeMetabelian G) :
    IsMetabelian G := by
  obtain ⟨X, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : IsMetabelian (FreeGroup X ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2) := by
    rw [IsMetabelian, ← map_derivedSeries_eq (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _),
      QuotientGroup.map_mk'_self]
  exact this.of_surjective (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom) e.symm.surjective

/-- A free metabelian group is projective in the variety of metabelian groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFreeMetabelian.isProjectiveMetabelian {G : Type u} [Group G]
    (h : IsFreeMetabelian G) : IsProjectiveMetabelian G := by
  refine ⟨h.isMetabelian, ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨X, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  intro A B _ _ hA _ f hf g
  set N := derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2
  choose a ha using fun x : X => hf (g (e.symm (QuotientGroup.mk (FreeGroup.of x))))
  have hker : N ≤ (FreeGroup.lift a).ker := by
    rw [← Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff, ← le_bot_iff, ← hA]
    exact map_derivedSeries_le_derivedSeries _ 2
  refine ⟨(QuotientGroup.lift N (FreeGroup.lift a) hker).comp e, ?_⟩
  have : f.comp (QuotientGroup.lift N (FreeGroup.lift a) hker) = g.comp e.symm := by
    refine QuotientGroup.monoidHom_ext N (FreeGroup.ext_hom _ _ fun x => ?_)
    simpa using ha x
  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x => ?_
  have h2 := DFunLike.congr_fun this (e x)
  rw [MonoidHom.comp_apply, MonoidHom.comp_apply] at h2
  simpa using h2

end Kourovka.«4.6»

items: 'Projective' is formalized by the lifting property against *surjective* homomorphisms between metabelian groups (the group-theoretic definition used by Hall/Neumann/Artamonov), rather than against categorical epimorphisms in the full subcategory of metabelian groups. This matches the decomposition notes ('every epimorphism from a metabelian group onto it splits' / 'retract of a free metabelian group'), and the two formulations (lifting property vs. retract of free) are equivalent by the standard pullback argument.

The lifting property in `IsProjectiveMetabelian` quantifies over test groups `A B` in the same universe as `P` (here `Type`). This is mathematically harmless: the lifting property against all metabelian groups is equivalent to being a retract of the free metabelian group on the underlying set of `P`, which lives in the same universe.

`IsMetabelian P` is included as a conjunct of `IsProjectiveMetabelian P` so that the group is required to lie in the variety; without it, absolutely free groups of rank ≥ 2 would satisfy the lifting property but are not metabelian.

`IsFreeMetabelian` uses an explicit isomorphism with `FreeGroup X ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup X) 2` with `X : Type u`. Since any basis of a free metabelian group in `Type` has cardinality ≤ |G|, restricting `X` to the same universe loses nothing. Rank 0 (trivial group) counts as free, matching the usual convention and the fact that the trivial group is projective.

`IsMetabelian` requires `IsMetabelian B` in the definition of projectivity even though it follows from `IsMetabelian A` and surjectivity of `f`; this redundancy keeps the definition literally 'in the variety' and is harmless.

Extra API/test lemmas (abelian ⇒ metabelian; images of metabelian groups are metabelian; F/F'' is free metabelian; free metabelian ⇒ metabelian ⇒ projective) are included with full proofs, per the repository's request to add basic API tests for bespoke definitions. They also confirm the question is not vacuous: every free metabelian group is projective, so `answer(True)` is a genuine 'yes'.

reviewer_notes: Modeling points a reviewer should know: (1) 'Epimorphism' is read as surjective homomorphism, the standard convention in the varieties-of-groups literature (Neumann, Hall, Artamonov: projective = retract of a relatively free group); categorical epis in the full subcategory of metabelian groups are not used. (2) Test groups in IsProjectiveMetabelian and the basis type in IsFreeMetabelian live in the same universe as the group; this is harmless (a projective P is a retract of the free metabelian group on P's carrier; a basis of F/F'' injects into F/F' so has cardinality ≤ |G|). Main quantifier over `Type` follows existing Kourovka files. (3) IsMetabelian B in the lifting definition is redundant (follows from IsMetabelian A and surjectivity) but harmless. (4) Rank 0 (trivial group) counts as free metabelian, matching convention; trivial group is projective, so no degenerate mismatch. Bespoke definitions (IsMetabelian, IsFreeMetabelian, IsProjectiveMetabelian) are kept in the problem file since the deliverable is a single file; a maintainer may wish to move IsMetabelian to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Other candidates were all faithful too; c01 (universal-property freeness, universe-polymorphic theorem), c03/c04/c06 (no API tests; c04 mixes Type*/Type universes, c06 relies on an autobound universe), c05/c07/c08 (fine, comparable to c02). No candidate omitted the slot.
